w: Arjunbhai Chavda had come from Ahmedabad to Mumbai to see how Swamishri's health was and to have his darshan. So that Swamishri would not be put to more strain and his treatment would not be disturbed, he had darshan and asked leave to go. Swamishri then instructed him to stay until Punam (full moon day). But Swamishri's way of pressing someone to stay was always unique.

Swamishri said to him, "Once you come to Mumbai, you cannot get out. Balmukunddas Swami used to say, 'From Kunkavav you cannot get out of the vav (stepwell). From Rajkot you cannot get out of the kot (fort). In the same way, from Mumbai too you cannot get out.'" Citing the words of a great sadhu, Swamishri bound Arjun Kaka to stay. Swamishri greatly understood the glory of such long-standing devotees of Shastriji Maharaj and made everyone understand it.

Then he said to Dhirubhai Bhatt, "Put it in the newspapers. The parayan (scripture discourse series) will be held on this date and will end on this date. Put it in 'Mumbai Samachar', 'Sandesh'... (drawing it out) and 'Bhumika Bapu' (Janmabhumi)." In this way he made everyone laugh.
Sadhu Ishwarcharandas

w: Swamishri performed the foundation stone laying ceremony with Vedic rites for the new Shikharbaddh mandir in Houston. The historic function had 102 main participants ('yajmans'), 750 couples and leading dignitaries during the maha-puja ceremony. An assembly followed after the rituals wherein dignitaries expressed their congratulations and good wishes for the mandir project. Mr. James Adolfse, a Fortband County judge, said, " I take this opportunity to invite His Holiness to come to Houston in a couple of years to open the traditional Hindu Temple. I pray to God and offer my best wishes for his excellent health. I have no doubt this temple will be an excellent monument due to your labor of love and of course the divine blessings of Pramukh Swami Maharaj."

Mr. Leonard Scarcella, Mayor of Stafford, expressed his feelings on the occasion, " I have no doubt in my mind that a beautiful temple will be built here. Your temple will serve everyone and raise the profile of team spirit and family values." In conclusion, Swamishri blessed the function, "Here in future an abode of our culture and a divine center of religion will be created. Along with our efforts in creating mandirs the important facet is that our own lives are inspired with spiritual values, honesty, non-violence, self-control, mutual love and compassion. And these values are attained through faith and devotion to God and obedience to the commands prescribed by our holy scriptures. This fundamental aspect of life is achieved through mandirs." In the later part of his blessings Swamishri elaborated upon the details of the Narmada Dam Project and its gigantic benefits to the water-starved areas of Kutch and Saurashtra. Swamishri also pointed out the misconceptions and false information being disseminated by some social workers protesting the project. As a firsthand observer of the project and the prevailing suffering due to the water crisis, Swamishri authentically spelled out the necessity of the project and appealed to all to sign a petition for the completion of the project that has been presently stalled by a court stay. In a matter of hours 11000 devotees and well-wishers signed the petition. Swamishri had appealed to the other BAPS centers and Indian organizations to sign the petition to be presented to the P.M. Vajpayee and officials of the International Rivers Network (IRN) in Washington DC.

Suvarna Samagam As an appreciation for the dedicated efforts of the Bal Mandal co-ordinators throughout the numerous Suvarna Jayanti programmes, a special programme titled 'Suvarna Samagam' was held. Senior sadhus addressed the assembly on the importance of Bal Mandal activities. The audience was inspired through captivating presentations and an animatronic murti of Yogiji Maharaj. Addressing the bal co-ordinators, Swamishri emphasised the need to live a pure and morally correct life.

Swamishri welcomed the vice-president of India, H.E. Shri Bhaironsingh Shekhawat, with a garland. He expressed his appreciations and praises for the creation of Akshar-dham. Thereafter the chairman of Metro Train, Shridharan, received Swamishri’s blessings.
The former Prime Minister of India Shri Deve Gowda was also welcomed and blessed by Swamishri.

Where, in what form, and for whom Pramukh Swami Maharaj fulfils wishes and gives joy is beyond description. Here, a boy named Parth Rathod lives in the Ambavadi area, and he is the only satsangi in his home. His parents are well disposed towards satsang. Since childhood, Parth of this middle class family had a wish: "I want to garland Swami Bapa." He had also read in 'Bal Prakash' that "Bapa fulfils the wishes of children." Because of all this reading, his longing was growing stronger and stronger. Just then Swamishri happened to come to Bhavnagar. Parth was overjoyed to hear this news. With the thought that Swamishri was to arrive on the 23rd, Parth said to his father, who has a shoe and sandal shop, "Today, when you come home from the shop, bring a flower garland for me. I want to garland Swami Bapa."

His father did say "yes", but because of the Raksha Bandhan festival there were so many customers at the shop that he closed the shop late and then went out to look for a garland. But since it was already two or three in the afternoon, he could not find a garland anywhere. So he came home empty handed. Parth asked his mother, "Where is the garland?" Then his mother told him the situation. So Parth said, "Give me the money. I will somehow get a flower garland."

He could not rest at night. He got up earlier than usual. Early in the morning, at 5:30, he set out to look for a garland. Parth, who was usually afraid even to go to tuition at 6:00, felt no fear at all today. On his bicycle he reached the areas where there were flower garland shops. He asked about garlands. No one sits selling garlands so early in the morning, but he went to a gardener's house and knocked on the door. When the door opened from inside, the boy said, "I want a flower garland to put on Pramukh Swami. Please make one for me." The gardener too, with feeling, gave him a big garland for fifteen rupees.

Taking the garland, he came with enthusiasm and joy to the Aksharvadi mandir, when it must have been only about 7:00! In the assembly hall, Viveksagar Swami's katha was going on. In his excitement he came that way with the bag containing the garland, when he saw Swami Bapa coming down from the lift in front of him. His joy knew no bounds. He ran towards him. Going up to Bapa, he offered the garland. Swamishri accepted his garland, gave it back to him as prasad, and instructed him to study well and to do puja regularly.
Taking that sanctified garland, with the joy that his wish had been fulfilled, he ran back, and then he learned that "Swami Bapa is still in his room. It is only 7:00." His amazement knew no bounds.

To fulfil a child's childhood wish, Swamishri accepted his devotion in his divine form. Otherwise the volunteers had already told him, "Swami Bapa does not accept anyone's garland like this, and he does not meet anyone except in the morning." This is Swamishri's unique way.

There was a letter from a spiritual seeker. He had sincerely written the details of all the mistakes he had made and asked for prayaschitt (atonement). After reading the letter, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "However much he does, there is no atonement for this. So write to him that if he keeps firm and observes niyam and dharma, things will be good from now on."

ds.t: More seva for those who bear it
w: Punyakirtan Swami said, "In activities one sees that the one who endures has to endure more and more. Among volunteers too, the one who wears himself out gets more seva."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "When there is the thought of pleasing God, it does not matter even if one is worn out more. Otherwise, even if you tell the other person, he will not do it, because it is not in his mind at all. He just stays with 'It happens, it goes on, it will do.' But the one who is keen to please God takes care in every way."

The sadhus were removing with a wet tissue the archa (sacred mark) that had been applied to Mahant Swami Maharaj's forehead in the morning. Swamishri said, "This is the fourth time Ishwarcharandas Swami has applied the archa."
Everyone was amazed! What things, and how much, Swamishri remembers!!

ds.t: Touching the feet of the paramhansas
w: Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the assembly, four pillars had been set up on the stage for the pujan (worship) of the first pillar of the "Paramhans Mandapam." Inside each was a paramhansa.

As Swamishri walked to the pillar near the throne, the paramhansa in it moved a little. Swamishri immediately looked up, and the paramhansa even smiled! Swamishri began looking at him with great joy and surprise, because Swamishri had thought that a murti of a paramhansa had been set in the pillar. But here a child was standing like a murti, dressed as a paramhansa.

This child dressed as a paramhansa had a garland in his hands, which he held out to put on Swamishri. Swamishri immediately began looking for Thakorji. From behind, the sadhus said, "Swami! It has been offered to Thakorji." Swamishri moved forward and the paramhansa stretched out his hands and placed the garland around Swamishri's neck. Swamishri reached out his hand to touch his feet... The child dressed as a paramhansa kept saying no, but Swamishri, out of reverence, did touch his feet!
Walking on, he came to the second pillar. Here too, Swamishri reverently touched the feet of the second living paramhansa adorning the pillar.
It was a wonderful, divine, heavenly and unforgettable sight!!
Swamishri bows to devotees all day long anyway, but on such occasions one feels that his real liking is to properly touch the feet of devotees.
